sections.label: Executors' unusual conditions
sections.summary: The executors, Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling, insisted on conditions including a $1 buy-back right and display of the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew's demolition wishes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The executors of the estate, namely, Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling, insisted on several unusual conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These conditions included (a) the right to buy back the items at $1, so long as the house was not demolished, and (b) the display of the wishes of the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew to demolish the house.

sections.label: NHB signs Deed with executors
sections.summary: NHB assessed several objects as deteriorated and needing immediate care and conservation, so it signed the Deed with the executors on 8 June 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: NHB also assessed that several of the objects were in a deteriorated condition and required immediate care and conservation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, NHB signed the Deed with the executors on 8 June 2015.

sections.label: Lee Hsien Yang calls request breach
sections.summary: Mr Lee Hsien Yang responded on 10 June that the request was unacceptable and would breach a legally-binding Deed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Mr Lee Hsien Yang responded on 10 June that this request was unacceptable and would be a breach of a legally-binding Deed.

sections.label: Probate not needed for Deed
sections.summary: On 12 June, Mr Lee Hsien Yang replied that the executors had not obtained probate but probate was not necessary for their power to enter the Deed of Gift.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: On 12 June, Mr Lee Hsien Yang replied to NHB that the executors had not obtained probate for the will but that probate was not necessary for the executors to have the power and authority to enter into the Deed of Gift.

sections.label: Exhibition pluses outweigh controversy
sections.summary: After weighing all factors and considering NHB had signed the Deed, Deputy Prime Minister Teo and the speaker agreed the exhibition's pluses outweighed likely controversy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, after weighing all the factors and considering that NHB had already signed the Deed, both Deputy Prime Minister Teo and I agreed that the pluses of having the exhibition with the Oxley Road artefacts in accordance with the Deed outweighed the potential controversy that was likely to arise.

sections.label: Exhibition opening date shifted
sections.summary: NHB could proceed with the exhibition with agreement from all beneficiaries, and the opening was shifted from 6 August to 21 September 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: NHB was thus able to proceed with the exhibition with agreement from all beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Eventually, the opening was shifted from 6 August to 21 September 2015.

sections.label: Deed of Gift confidentiality
sections.summary: The Deed of Gift did not have a confidentiality clause, in response to Assoc Prof Daniel Goh's question.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In response to the question from Assoc Prof Daniel Goh, the Deed of Gift did not have a confidentiality clause.

sections.label: Preservation of Monuments Act
sections.summary: Under the Preservation of Monuments Act, a gazetted residence must be acquired within one year or the preservation order lapses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Under the Preservation of Monuments Act, if a building is occupied as a residence and the Government chooses to gazette it as a monument, then the Government has to acquire it within one year of the preservation order or else the preservation order will lapse.

sections.label: Ministerial Committee on 38 Oxley Road
sections.summary: A Ministerial Committee was set up to coordinate agencies and draw up options for 38 Oxley Road, with no preconceived notion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Later, in discussing the matter with the Deputy Prime Minister and various Ministerial colleagues, we agreed that it would be useful to have a Ministerial Committee to coordinate the work across agencies and to oversee the matter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why MND tabled the proposal at the Cabinet meeting chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Teo on 1 June to set up the Ministerial Committee to draw up a range of possible options for 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As the Deputy Prime Minister said earlier, the Ministerial Committee has no preconceived notion on what to do with the property.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But the current Government has the duty to do the work now in listing out all the options and to prepare ahead of the implications of each one of them.

sections.label: Demolition of Mr Lee's home
sections.summary: The core issue is whether Mr Lee's private home should be demolished according to his personal wishes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: At its heart lies the issue of whether the private home of Mr Lee should be demolished in accordance with his personal wishes.

sections.label: Ministerial Committee and Mr Lee's wishes
sections.summary: The question is whether the Government should have set up the Ministerial Committee to consider options possibly against Mr Lee's wishes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The question is whether the Government should have set up the Ministerial Committee and placed itself in the position to consider options that may not be in line with the late Mr Lee's personal wishes.

sections.label: Allegations against Prime Minister and Cabinet
sections.summary: The sitting addresses serious allegations against the Prime Minister and Cabinet for abuse of power and manipulation of State Organs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: We are not here to settle family disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: We are here today to address the serious allegations made against the Prime Minister and Cabinet for abuse of power and manipulation of State Organs for personal needs.

sections.label: Oxley Road debate and national agenda
sections.summary: The passage says the Prime Minister's Statement answers allegations, that the family matters are private, and that after the debate the Government must press on with the national agenda.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister's Statement today provides the answers needed to Singaporeans to clear the allegations of abuse of power and manipulation of State Organs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The issues relating to the late Mr Lee's personal wishes regarding 38 Oxley Road, his last will and testament, as well as the dispute between family members, are private personal family matters and should rightly remain so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: However, as pointed out by many Singaporeans leading up to the debate, Dr Lee Wei Ling and Mr Lee Hsien Yang are not present in this House to participate in this debate today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Singaporeans are concerned that a further protraction of this saga will harm and detract Singapore from other far more pressing and urgent national and international issues that confront us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Once the allegations against the Prime Minister and the Cabinet have been put to rest after this debate, our Government must press ahead with our national agenda.

sections.label: Blurred private and public line
sections.summary: The passage states the private and public line was blurred and crossed by the Prime Minister, the Lee siblings and the Government, and that the saga distracts and damages the Singapore brand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The problem with this whole saga is that the line between the private and the public has been blurred and crossed too many times by the Prime Minister, the Lee siblings and the Government, too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We need to do this so as to move on for far more important issues that are truly national issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This saga is distracting the Government, distracting Singaporeans, distracting the international audience and damaging the Singapore brand.

sections.label: Conflict of interest question
sections.summary: The passage asks whether there is a conflict of interest there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Is there not a conflict of interest there?

sections.label: Another conflict of interest question
sections.summary: The passage asks whether there is also a conflict of interest here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Is there also a conflict of interest here?

sections.label: Court as correct platform
sections.summary: The passage states the view that the correct platform to settle the private dispute is the Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, I am of the view that the correct platform to settle the private dispute is the Court.

sections.label: Government power over 38 Oxley Road
sections.summary: The passage states the Government has the power under the law to decide what to do with 38 Oxley Road, as Deputy Prime Minister Teo said.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, the Government has the power under the law to decide what to do with 38 Oxley Road, as what Deputy Prime Minister Teo has said.

sections.label: Need for Ministerial Committee questioned
sections.summary: The speaker asks why a Ministerial Committee is needed when the Government can act decisively in the national interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Why is there a need for a Ministerial Committee to look into this when the Government clearly has the power to act decisively in the national interest?

sections.label: Reputation, credibility and authority at stake
sections.summary: The speaker says the country's reputation, the Prime Minister's credibility and the Government's authority are at stake and urges quick resolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The country's reputation is at stake, the Prime Minister's credibility has been called into question and the Government's authority has been undermined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I urge the Prime Minister and the Cabinet to do whatever is necessary to bring this dispute to a quick resolution.

sections.label: Oxley Road dispute and Government work
sections.summary: The speaker says private citizens allege abuse of power, and hopes leaders can get on with work like childcare, seniors, MRTs and defence.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: Ms Sun, you have only one minute left.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: And he would only reconsider his position to leave Singapore if the Prime Minister were no longer in a position of power.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: It appears that he wants to bring down the Prime Minister.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: A clarification becomes an act of aggression, cleaning the house becomes intermeddling and theft.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We will have to make a conscious choice if we want the energies of our Prime Minister and other Ministers named in the saga to spend their time addressing allegations levelled at them over Facebook anytime of the day, but there are childcare centres to be built, seniors to be taken care of, MRTs that need to be looked into, our homeland and cybersecurity defended and economic restructuring to be carried out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: There is work to be done, dogsbody work, and I hope our political leaders and the Government can get on with it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On the fundamental level, the 38 Oxley Road case is one whereby private citizens, namely, Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling, are alleging that the Prime Minister and the Government are abusing their powers.

sections.label: Preservation Board versus Ministerial Committee
sections.summary: The speaker asks why a Ministerial Committee is needed when the Preservation of Sites and Monuments Board can decide on 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Why must a Ministerial Committee be set up when we have the Preservation of Sites and Monuments Board which can decide on whether 38 Oxley Road should be preserved, demolished or any other options?

sections.label: Public inquiry through Select Committee
sections.summary: The speaker asks Parliament to consider a public inquiry, possibly a Parliamentary Select Committee, so all parties' allegations are scrutinised equally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As such, I would like for Parliament to consider setting up a public inquiry on this matter, maybe through a Parliamentary Select Committee, so that all parties involved can have their allegations and statements articulated and scrutinised equally.

sections.label: Independent ombudsman for disputes
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Government consider an independent ombudsman to deal with future disputes between private parties and the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is a case when the private and the Government disagree.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And maybe I would suggest for the Government to consider seriously setting up an independent ombudsman to deal with such disputes in future whenever they arise.

sections.label: Loss of national heritage
sections.summary: The loss of national heritage can be very emotional, and society has had to accept decisions and move on, though the Deputy Prime Minister acknowledged past work was overzealous.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The loss of our national heritage, whether the National Library, the National Theatre, dragon playground or Bukit Brown Cemetery, can be very emotional, affecting not just the mind but the heart and soul of the people involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Society has had to accept the decisions and just move on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I was very glad to hear the Deputy Prime Minister acknowledging that, in the past, such work has been overzealous.

sections.label: 38 Oxley Road decision
sections.summary: It asks whether a decision on 38 Oxley Road can be made with wisdom and clarity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the case of 38 Oxley Road, can a decision be made with wisdom and clarity?

sections.label: Wills and family disputes
sections.summary: It asks whether family members should be part of the will-making process, since obstacles and feelings can seed future disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Such obstacles, combined with feelings of pride and fear and blindness, can lead to decisions that seed future disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And so, in future, when wills are being made, should we not consider having this possibility whereby family members should be part of the process and maybe be a requirement?

sections.label: Allegations affecting leadership integrity
sections.summary: It states that the allegations can affect the integrity of the leadership and Government and people's confidence, and should be addressed firmly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The allegations that were made can affect the integrity of the leadership and also the Government, as well as the people's confidence, and this should be addressed firmly.

sections.label: Addressing abuse of power allegations
sections.summary: It hopes the session can address allegations about the Government's abuse of power and conflict of interest involving the Prime Minister in 38 Oxley Road matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Although I do not think that this session can resolve the dispute, however, as many Singaporeans have wished for, it is hoped that this session can address the various allegations about the Government's abuse of power and any conflict of interest amongst those who are involved, including the Prime Minister, in the matters related to 38 Oxley Road.

sections.label: Malay and English speeches
sections.summary: It states the first matter will be covered in the Malay speech and the rest in English, and that forming a Ministerial committee is normal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I will touch on the first matter in my Malay speech, and the rest in my English speech later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I understand that the formation of a Ministerial committee is a normal thing as the Cabinet forms Ministerial committees on many strategic matters.

sections.label: No decision while Lee Wei Ling resides
sections.summary: The Ministerial Committee and Prime Minister committed that no decision will be taken while Dr Lee Wei Ling resides in the house.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the end, after the sequence of events have become clearer, based on the facts presented, we are more informed that the Ministerial Committee and the Prime Minister have given the commitment that no decision will be taken as long as Dr Lee Wei Ling still resides in the house.

sections.label: Oxley Road house remains intact
sections.summary: The Government assured that 38 Oxley Road will remain intact as long as Dr Lee Wei Ling lives there, respecting Mr Lee Kuan Yew's wish.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But at the heart of it all, amidst all the attention and information being shared by many quarters, the one question that I was left to grapple with was: what was the issue about in the first place?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We know that according to the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew, the house need not be demolished until his daughter chooses not to live in it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Government is also clear that it will respect Mr Lee's wish in this regard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, it is not as if a decision was taken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We have been assured before by the Government that as long as Dr Lee Wei Ling continues to live in 38 Oxley Road, it shall remain intact.

sections.label: Lee family exemption from Government decisions
sections.summary: The member says exempting Lee family members from Government deliberations due to their standing sets wrong principles and precedence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If some members of the Lee family believe that they should be exempted from Government deliberations or decisions just because they are a family of standing, then I think this sets the wrong principles and precedence.

sections.label: Late Mr Lee's last will accuracy
sections.summary: The member seeks clarification on the late Mr Lee's last will and how far the Government should be involved in determining its accuracy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The third area that I seek clarification on is on the matter of the last will of the late Mr Lee and the extent to which the Government should be involved in determining its accuracy.

sections.label: Prime Minister's capacity for comment
sections.summary: The member suggests the Prime Minister clarify in which capacity he made a comment, to clarify the Government's perceived role.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Perhaps it may be useful for the Prime Minister to clarify in which capacity he made this comment as it would then clarify the Government's perceived role in it.

sections.label: Handling further Lee family queries
sections.summary: The member asks how the Government will handle further Lee family queries and when Parliament will consider further enquiry or a select committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How does the Government plan to handle communications and further clarifications from the Lee family if there are still queries beyond what has been explained today?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under what circumstances will the Government or Parliament consider further enquiry or a select committee to investigate any further allegations or disputes of accounts?

sections.label: Attorney-General prosecutorial discretion power
sections.summary: The Attorney-General is described as a powerful state actor with almost absolute prosecutorial discretion, more powerful than Judges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The AG is a fiercely powerful state actor, more powerful than our Judges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: By contrast, the AG, as the Public Prosecutor, has almost absolute prosecutorial discretion.

sections.label: Attorney-General ties to Lee estate
sections.summary: The Attorney-General was a long-time senior partner of the Law Minister and had advised the Prime Minister on Lee estate matters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As for the AG, it was also well-known that he had been a senior partner in the same firm as the Law Minister for a long time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We now learn from the Lee siblings that the AG also happened to be the Prime Minister's personal lawyer, and that he had advised the Prime Minister specifically on the matters relating to the Lee estate.

sections.label: Attorney-General recusal question
sections.summary: It asks whether the Attorney-General recused himself after representing the Prime Minister as a beneficiary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Has the AG recused himself from even touching the file, since he had represented Prime Minister Lee in his personal capacity as a beneficiary?

sections.label: Powers over Lee estate matters
sections.summary: It raises whether the Prime Minister, Ministers and Attorney-General exercised powers properly, warning of eroding public trust in state institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Another thread is whether the Prime Minister, other Ministers and the AG had exercised their powers properly in handling matters touching on the Lee estate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My concern is on the latter, particularly how we protect the rule of law and our institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Let us be most alive to the risk of a slippery slope that erodes public trust in the independence of our Organs of State.

sections.label: Questions on organs of state
sections.summary: It asks whether organs of state, the Prime Minister's power and the Singapore press were used against Lee Wei Ling and Lee Hsien Yang.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Dr Lee Wei Ling and Mr Lee Hsien Yang have said, "We fear the use of the Organs of State against us and Hsien Yang's wife, Suet Fern." My question: is it true or false that the Organs of State are being abused to target Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Second, "  Wei Ling and   Hsien Yang question whether able leaders with independent political legitimacy will be sidelined to ensure Hsien Loong's grip on power remains unchallenged." Is it true that ensuring the Prime Minister's power remains unchallenged, if that is at all true, trumps independent political legitimacy?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Third, to the South China Morning Post (SCMP), Mr Lee Hsien Yang has said, "A few of the attacks that we have had to face in private are now public − false accusations, character assassinations, the entire machinery of the Singapore press thrown against us." Is it true or false that the Government has used the Singapore press to target Dr Lee Wei Ling and Mr Lee Hsien Yang?

sections.label: Question on lying to Parliament
sections.summary: It asks whether the Prime Minister lied to Parliament, citing Lee Hsien Yang's statement about a contradiction with a statutory declaration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Ninth, on 15 June 2017 at 9.25 pm, Mr Lee Hsien Yang wrote, "Hsien Loong's public statement to Parliament contradicts the statutory declaration he made to his secret committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It is wrong to lie to Parliament and it is wrong to lie under oath." My question: is it true or false that the Prime Minister lied to Parliament?

sections.label: Allegations of abuse of power
sections.summary: The allegations by Mr Lee and Dr Lee insinuate abuse of power and that Organs of State pursue agendas beyond their mission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In short, the insinuations of Mr Lee's and Dr Lee's allegations are that there has been an abuse of power and that the Organs of State carry out agendas beyond the scope of their mission.

sections.label: Allegations must be aired and debated
sections.summary: The governance system must last for generations and be held in high regard, so the allegations must be aired, debated and answered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It must be so, for this system of governance must last for generations to come and must be held in high regard by Singaporeans through that course.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: That is why these allegations must be aired, debated, answered to.

sections.label: Duty to constituents and Parliament
sections.summary: The speaker has a sacred duty to constituents and, as an elected Parliamentarian and Government Parliamentary Committee Chair, must ask tough questions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, I also have a sacred duty to the constituents I represent and serve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, it is incumbent on me and my duty as an elected Parliamentarian and Government Parliamentary Committee Chair for the Ministries of Home Affairs and Law to ask the tough questions.

sections.label: Protecting confidence in Government system
sections.summary: What matters most is the continued good reputation of the system of Government and Singaporeans' confidence in the system built by Mr Lee Kuan Yew and the founding fathers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What is of foremost importance to me is the continued good reputation of our system of Government and that Singaporeans continue to have confidence in that system, a system built by Mr Lee Kuan Yew and our founding fathers, a system we have a deep duty to advance and to protect.

sections.label: Exhibition items and unusual conditions
sections.summary: The exhibition received items from the estate executors under two unusual conditions concerning buy-back at $1 and display of part of the demolition clause.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As Minister Lawrence Wong mentioned just now, this exhibition received items from the executors of the estate, Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling, under two unusual conditions.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One was that the executors of the estate could buy back all the items at $1 as long as 38 Oxley Road was not demolished.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second was that part of the demolition clause from the late Minister Mentor Lee's will, the part that expressed the wish for immediate demolition of the house after Dr Lee Wei Ling moves out of it should be prominently displayed, whereas the other part of the will outlining what was to be done if the house could not be demolished was to be omitted from the exhibition.

sections.label: Government role and Minister Mentor's wishes
sections.summary: The speaker asks what this has to do with the Government and how much weight Minister Mentor Lee's wishes bear on the Oxley House Ministerial Committee's decisions.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, now, what has it to do with the Government?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Also, in view of Minister Mentor Lee's latest will which is with the demolition clause, how much weight will Minister Mentor Lee's wishes bear on the decisions to be made by the Oxley House Ministerial Committee?

sections.label: Lee Hsien Yang corruption allegations
sections.summary: Mr Lee Hsien Yang is making damning allegations of political corruption, state intimidation and nepotism.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The allegations of abuse of political corruption, state intimidation and nepotism being made by Mr Lee Hsien Yang are damning.

sections.label: Independent hearing for PM accusers
sections.summary: The powerful should be bound by the same rules, and the Prime Minister's accusers should have an independent Select Committee or Commission of Inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The powerful must be bound by the same principles, values and rules that the less powerful are being asked to play by.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I agree with the WP's approach that "the crux of the family issues surrounding 38 Oxley Road is for the family to resolve privately or in Court" and that Parliament should only be "concerned with the allegations of abuse of power and the harms these have caused to confidence in Singapore and our political institutions." The Prime Minister's accusers should have an independent, neutral space where they can be held to account for their words, put down their side of the story on official record, sharing whatever arguments and evidence they have to back their claims.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Such a hearing can happen either as an independent Select Committee, or a Commission of Inquiry (COI), which would have full authority to investigate the accusations, to summon evidence surrounding the most biting allegations raised in the original "What has happened to Lee Kuan Yew's values?" document about the supposed misuse of power by the Prime Minister and his wife, the supposed Orwellian threat of state intimidation and monitoring of private citizens, and the supposed nepotism behind key appointments in the Public Service.

sections.label: Lee Hsien Yang on parliamentary forum
sections.summary: Mr Lee Hsien Yang believes the Parliamentary session places the Prime Minister before subordinates lacking background and evidence, so a Committee of Inquiry is hoped for.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Lee Hsien Yang has already made it clear to the many Singaporeans following his Facebook posts that he believes "This Parliamentary session is a forum that again places the Prime Minister before his subordinates" who "lack sufficient background and evidence of the numerous instances of abuse and conflicts of interest, many yet to be raised".

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That is why I hope the Prime Minister will consider subjecting himself to an independent Committee of Inquiry on the allegations made against him and his Government.

sections.label: Independent committee for statutory declarations
sections.summary: Since the Prime Minister made a statutory declaration, an independent Committee could request his accusers also offer theirs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since the Prime Minister has already made a statutory declaration, it would be most fair and helpful for Singaporeans to have an independent Committee set up that can request that his accusers would also offer theirs.

sections.label: Oxley not a major suggestion
sections.summary: Oxley never came up as a major suggestion; more public spaces like Fort Canning or Singapore River were wanted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Incidentally, Oxley never actually came up as a major suggestion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They wanted more public spaces like Fort Canning or Singapore River.

sections.label: Lee Hsien Yang open to memorial garden
sections.summary: Mr Lee Hsien Yang seems open to the memorial garden idea.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Lee Hsien Yang seems open to that memorial garden idea.

sections.label: Family narratives and resilience
sections.summary: Psychologists found families with oscillating narratives, not other kinds, produced the most resilient children, and open talk of past wounds may make the country resilient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But what was interesting is psychologists discovered that both these kinds of families are not resilient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is those families that tell an oscillating narrative instead − a roller-coaster trajectory of a tale with ups and downs − that consistently produced the most resilient children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The oscillating family story helps them develop a strong "intergenerational self", a purposeful awareness that they are part of something larger than themselves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many want this conversation full of suffering to just end.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope we do not artificially shut down the conversation because learning to talk about our biggest mistakes, our darkest imperfections, our most painful wounds from our past is precisely what our younger generations need right now as a country if we hope to be resilient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If this event helps us start to talk more openly about how things work in our country and how we want things to work in our country, the good and the bad, it is possible for us to come out of this saga even stronger as a people.

sections.label: Options and land value
sections.summary: The Government highlighted conservation, preservation and land acquisition options worth around $20 million, while redevelopment with rezoning could raise land value far higher.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Government has highlighted various options − conservation, preservation and land acquisition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I have heard that these options are worth around $20 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Now, if full demolition and redevelopment happen in the future, and if URA under the future government agrees to rezoning, the land could be worth a lot more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I believe a piece of land nearby was recently sold for more than $100 million.

sections.label: Prime Minister recusal question
sections.summary: It asks whether the Prime Minister recused himself and whether Deputy Prime Minister Teo proposed the Ministerial Committee in his absence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Did the Prime Minister recuse himself, and did Deputy Prime Minister Teo, as the leader of the Cabinet in the Prime Minister's absence, propose the Ministerial Committee?

sections.label: Two upcoming Bills
sections.summary: After the Ministerial Statement debate, Parliament will discuss the MAS Act and the Home Team Corps Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: After we finish the debating on this Ministerial Statement, Parliament will discuss two more important Bills: one, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) Act that would keep our financial system intact when the next global financial crisis strikes; and two, the Home Team Corps Bill that would strengthen our people's support for a safe Singapore.

sections.label: Defamation suits and moral authority
sections.summary: Damages have been awarded over unsubstantiated defamatory allegations against politicians to preserve moral authority, and the anomaly is the Prime Minister not suing despite serious allegations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Millions of dollars in damages have been awarded when unsubstantiated allegations amounting to defamation and slander have been made against politicians, so as to preserve their moral authority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As recently as 2008, the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew himself said, and I quote, "I know the mentality of and the attitudes of the people in Singapore − and they know me by now, that if anybody impugns the integrity of the Government, of which I was the Prime Minister, I must sue….And I must demand that either the Court finds that those defamatory words (are) true, in which case, I am demolished, or there is a penalty." The anomaly in this matter before the House today surrounds the decision taken by the Prime Minister − ironically it must be said − not to sue in spite of the serious allegations of abuse of power, much to the surprise of many Singaporeans.

sections.label: Courts to rebut allegations
sections.summary: The Prime Minister has to go to the Courts to rebut allegations of abuse of power and decisively settle the issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister has to go to the Courts to rebut these allegations of abuse of power in order to decisively settle this issue.

sections.label: PM Goh finds no wrongdoing
sections.summary: Prime Minister Goh was convinced by his investigation that there was no wrongdoing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In view of his investigation, Prime Minister Goh was convinced that there was no wrongdoing.

sections.label: Proposed Select Committee on allegations
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a special Select Committee to look into allegations against the Prime Minister and summon witnesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the event the Prime Minister eschews going to the Courts to address these allegations of abuse of power even as more allegations are made and left to the people's imagination to ruminate over, I am of the view that the next best option would be for Parliament to prepare to organise a special Select Committee to look into the allegations made against the Prime Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Its remit would simply be to look into the truthfulness of the allegations and get to the bottom of the matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In light of evidence being made available to it, the Committee can be expected to summon, if it so chooses, the Prime Minister, Mdm Ho Ching, Mrs Lee Suet Fern and anyone else to shed light on the allegations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I make this proposal for a Select Committee of Parliament in the public interest as I believe it is an avenue to put a stop to these allegations which have now moved beyond damaging just the Government but have damaged Singapore's reputation and the trust people outside Singapore have in its institutions.

sections.label: Allegations question Government integrity
sections.summary: Allegations of abuse of power by Organs of State put the Government's integrity into question.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What started out as a "private family matter" is no longer just that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The allegations of the abuse of power by the Organs of State put into question the integrity of the Government, and this is serious.

sections.label: Ministerial Committee on 38 Oxley Road
sections.summary: The Ministerial Committee was convened in July last year to look into options for 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Ministerial Committee was convened in July last year, as shared by Deputy Prime Minister Teo, and the Ministerial Committee has been set up to look into various options for what happens to the house 38 Oxley Road and the implications of these options.

sections.label: PM recused from 38 Oxley Road
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said he recused himself from all Government decisions on 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Prime Minister, you have said that you have recused yourself from all Government decisions to be taken on 38 Oxley Road.

sections.label: Parliament does not preclude outside action
sections.summary: Coming to Parliament does not preclude anything else happening outside of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The first point I want to make is that coming to Parliament does not preclude anything else happening outside of Parliament.

sections.label: Parliament debating government process concerns
sections.summary: The speaker asks how Singapore could move forward if Parliament has lingering suspicion about its process of government and Members' authority to debate pressing problems.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Nothing else could have happened in two weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: But if it comes to Parliament, as we have done today, and we have to debate the Home Team Corps Bill, which I will be speaking on sometime after this debate – if we have to debate about issues to do with our finances, about MAS or other Statutory Boards and we have a lingering suspicion about our process of Government, about the authority of the Members of this House to debate, to analyse, to deal with the most pressing problems facing Singapore – how could we have gone forward?

sections.label: Parliament as appropriate place
sections.summary: The passage states that a report goes to Parliament, Parliament acts on its recommendations, and Parliament cannot be called an inappropriate place for these matters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Ultimately, it provides a report to Parliament and the actions taken on its recommendations are done by Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: So, if we are going to choose these routes, the one thing we cannot do, is say that Parliament is not the appropriate place to deal with these matters.

sections.label: Accountability through chain of command
sections.summary: Accountability extends through the whole chain of command, and a code of conduct and processes must be understood by every officer, with records available to Courts, a Select Committee or MPs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Accountability not just at the top − it has to be especially at the top, the Prime Minister has talked about that − but accountability extends all the way through.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This code of conduct, these values and these processes need to be understood by every officer in that chain of command so that they know when they are being asked to do something inappropriate, that they know that they have alternative lines of reporting, that they know that they can document these things and it will be there as a matter of record for the Courts, for a special Select Committee or for MPs to access, demonstrate and debate.

sections.label: Reason needed for Select Committee
sections.summary: The passage states that having a Select Committee requires some reason, rather than just saying one could not do the job properly, and that the allegations are important and serious.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: If we are going to have a Select Committee, you need to have some reason to have this Select Committee as opposed to just saying, "I was not able to do my job properly." These are important and serious allegations.

sections.label: Private citizen suing his brother
sections.summary: Parliament cannot make a private citizen sue his own brother; that choice belongs to the private citizen.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Parliament cannot make a private citizen sue his own brother; that is a choice for a private citizen to make.

sections.label: WP and MPs agreement
sections.summary: The passage states that WP and other MPs agree the matter should go back into the private space because there are no substantive allegations on abuse of power.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: There are some things that WP and all the other MPs agree on.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: That this is something that really should go away and back into the private space because there are no substantive allegations on the issues of the abuse of power.

sections.label: Select Committee and sound bite
sections.summary: A Select Committee will not end this now, and "End this saga now" is described as a throwaway sound bite.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: A Select Committee is not going to end this now. "End this saga now" is a very nice throwaway sound bite.

sections.label: Calls to end saga now
sections.summary: The passage urges ending the saga now by stating satisfaction with explanations given and understanding governance and Parliamentary democracy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: End this saga now because you are satisfied because you have not been able to bring any evidence to bear.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: End this saga now by standing up here and saying that you are satisfied with the explanations that have been given, that you understand the process of governance and Government and Parliamentary democracy.

sections.label: Law, Constitution and Speaker
sections.summary: The law and Constitution, represented by the Speaker, are the stone against which politicians, parties and Singaporeans sharpen positions and thoughts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The stone against which we have to sharpen our positions and our thoughts and achieve some clarity on where we are as politicians, as parties, as individual Singaporeans, is a combination of the law and our Constitution as represented by you, Mdm Speaker.

sections.label: House closing matter next day
sections.summary: It is contingent on the House to close this matter over the next day.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: It is contingent upon us to do that.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: And that is how, we need, as a House, to close this matter over the next day.

sections.label: Rule of law and due process
sections.summary: In all deliberations, whether on 38 Oxley Road or Sungei Road Hawker Zone, the rule of law and due process must prevail.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Because it is my conviction that in all deliberations, whether now or in the future, whether we are referring to 38 Oxley Road or whether we are referring to Sungei Road Hawker Zone, we must remember that under all circumstances, the rule of law and due process must prevail.

sections.label: Lee's wishes and due process
sections.summary: Mr Lee's wishes justify a Ministerial Committee, but the house should not be demolished solely because he wished it, and due process and country's interests must be considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Indeed, we must give due weight to Mr Lee's wishes and, for that, I see that there is a justification for a Ministerial Committee, but it is also just for us to understand his reasons as to why he made certain wishes known.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My own thinking is that it would not be right for us to demolish the house solely because he wished it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Mr Lee that I grew up knowing and respecting would not put his personal interests above the interests of his country.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There must be due process, we must consider the interests of the country as opposed to the wishes of a family.

sections.label: Rule of law assurance sought
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will assure Parliament it upholds the rule of law, and is disappointed national issues are not the focus.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But what I hope we can do today is that we can see for ourselves more clearly that there are certain issues that are none of our business, and certain issues that we need to clear the air.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And I hope that by the end of this debate, Prime Minister, you and your Government will give to us the assurance that we can always rely on this Government to uphold and to maintain the rule of law in Singapore because, without that, there is no way we can have the confidence that we would be able to look after our people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I feel deeply disappointed that, at a time like this, we are not focusing on national issues that matter so much to our people.

sections.label: Debate on Singapore's future
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the House remembers it is deciding Singapore's future, built by generations of Singaporeans' sacrifices, not one man.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I do not know what people a few generations later will think about this debate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I simply hope that when we step out of this House and end this debate today, we will go out remembering that we are not here just to talk about the institutions, our Prime Minister, the Deputy Prime Minister or his Ministers, but we are here debating and deciding on the future of Singapore − a Singapore that was not built by one man, not founded by the sacrifice of one man, but by the sacrifices of generations of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And, for that, I hope that we will not, never, allow that sacrifice to be in vain.

sections.label: Section 11 preservation orders
sections.summary: Section 11 states the Minister may, after consulting the Board, make a preservation order placing a monument under the Board's protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 11 states that "the Minister may, after consulting the Board, make a preservation order to place any monument under the protection of the Board." The "Board" here refers to the National Heritage Board.

sections.label: Section 9 conservation areas
sections.summary: Section 9 of the Planning Act lets the Minister designate an area a conservation area, with no mention of a Ministerial Committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If the plan is to conserve the area, then, similarly, section 9 of the Planning Act states, "Where in the opinion of the Minister any area is of special architectural, historic, traditional or aesthetic interest, the Minister may approve under section 8 a proposal to amend the Master Plan to designate the area as a conservation area." There is no mention of the role of a Ministerial Committee here in this piece of legislation as well.

sections.label: Ministerial Committees convening clarified
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Prime Minister to clarify when Ministerial Committees are convened and whether written rules govern them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Fourth, can the Prime Minister clarify under what circumstances are Ministerial Committees convened?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Are there written rules and procedures governing the setting up and functions of such committees?

sections.label: Objection to gazetting Oxley Road
sections.summary: The speaker records opposition to gazetting 38 Oxley Road, calling the house a private family matter, and cites a 2015 poll.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: From the accounts given by the Prime Minister today, the fate of the house is really a family matter and it should not be outsourced to the Government to decide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: I wish to put on record that I do not support the effort or intention of the Government to gazette 38 Oxley Road for whatever reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: A reported poll on 23 December 2015 indicated that 77% of the people said they would want to see Mr Lee Kuan Yew's wish for the house to be carried out, although I am of the opinion that such a poll is not even necessary, as this is a completely private matter for the immediate family members to sort out.

sections.label: Attorney-General was PM's lawyer
sections.summary: Sylvia Lim highlighted that Singaporeans learned the newly-appointed Attorney-General, Lucien Wong, was previously the Prime Minister's personal lawyer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: As highlighted by Ms Sylvia Lim, Singaporeans woke up in the morning to find out that our newly-appointed AG, Mr Lucien Wong, was also the personal lawyer of the Prime Minister previously.

sections.label: Allegations against PM's wife
sections.summary: Singaporeans learned the same morning of allegations that the Prime Minister's wife exerted influence beyond her job purview, which neither refuted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Singaporeans also found out the same morning that the wife of the Prime Minister was alleged to have exerted her influence on the Government and Civil Service in a pervasive manner and "well beyond her job purview." Neither the Prime Minister nor his wife has come out to refute the allegation in no uncertain terms.

sections.label: Safeguards against family members' influence
sections.summary: It asks what safeguards exist to prevent Ministers' family members from abusing positions of influence in engaging the Civil Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: While there is a code of conduct to govern Ministers, what safeguards are there to prevent their family members from abusing their positions of influence in their engagement with the Civil Service?

sections.label: Ho Ching listed as PMO contact
sections.summary: It asks what official role the Prime Minister's wife has in Government allowing her to act as a PMO contact person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: In an NHB document released on Facebook, a certain "Ms Ho Ching" was listed as a contact person for PMO, and Mr Lee Hsien Yang had alleged that this person is the wife of the Prime Minister, Mdm Ho Ching, of which, she did not deny.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: So, what official role does the wife of the Prime Minister have in Government that would allow her to act as a contact person for PMO?

sections.label: Addressing influence abuse allegations urgently
sections.summary: It asks whether the Prime Minister agrees the allegations of family members abusing positions of influence need urgent, emphatic, transparent addressing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Does the Prime Minister not agree that these allegations of abuse of position of influence by family members need to be addressed urgently and emphatically in a transparent manner?

sections.label: Questions on 38 Oxley Road committee
sections.summary: It states the rule of law is about due process, and residents have questions about the Ministerial Committee looking at 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The rule of law is also about due process.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And there are questions to be asked, that my residents have asked, about the Ministerial Committee looking at 38 Oxley Road.

sections.label: Ministerial Committee studying Lee Kuan Yew's will
sections.summary: Residents asked why a Ministerial Committee is studying Mr Lee Kuan Yew's will, and it is important to find out why.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Some of my residents have also asked, why should this Ministerial Committee be studying Mr Lee Kuan Yew's will?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is going to be very important to find out why exactly was this Ministerial Committee looking at the will, given what has been said online and given the concerns that many of my residents have raised.

sections.label: Intergenerational heritage equity
sections.summary: There is an issue of intergenerational heritage equity to think about, just as with fiscal Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Just as we have thought very carefully about our fiscal Reserves and how choices made by one generation should not over-commit the next generation, likewise, there is an issue of intergenerational heritage equity that we have to think about as well.

sections.label: Call to show evidence
sections.summary: Those alleging abuse of power online are asked to show their evidence and bring it all out.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: If I may say to those who have been alleging abuse of power, those who have been making online allegations: show us the evidence, bring it all out.

sections.label: Singapore deserves better
sections.summary: All are sons and daughters of Singapore, which deserves a lot better than what happened at 2.00 am on 14 June.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: But all of us are sons and daughters of Singapore, the Singapore that Mr Lee and his Pioneer generation built.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And our Singapore deserves a lot better than what happened at 2.00 am on 14 June this year.

sections.label: Hope for reconciliation and healing
sections.summary: The speaker hopes today's divisions can be reconciled, the pain and sadness healed, and Singapore come through stronger.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: But tomorrow is still ours to shape, our days of present futures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, I hope with all my heart that today's divisions can somehow be reconciled, that the pain and sadness felt throughout so much of Singapore can and will be healed, and that whatever happens, our Singapore, our country, will come through this stronger and better than before.

sections.label: Clarification on demolition and cult worshipping
sections.summary: The speaker asks which part of the speech says the house should be demolished in haste, and says he is not into cult worshipping.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: Which part of my speech says that I want the house to be demolished in a haste?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: I believe the Hansard will reflect that my understanding of Mr Png's speech was that he was alluding to a certain point of view.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: That seems to be quite a possibly natural conclusion to draw from the points he was making.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Will Mr Png reply to my clarification as well, please?

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: I will send the speech later and it will be in the Hansard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: In reply to his question, I am not into cult worshipping.

sections.label: Probate granted without protest
sections.summary: A grant of probate was made without protest on 6 October 2015, more than six months earlier.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: After all, a grant of probate was made without protest on 6 October 2015, more than six months ago.

sections.label: Parliamentary Select Committee consideration
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a Parliamentary Select Committee was ever considered before the Cabinet Committee was organised, noting Standing Order 101 allows bipartisan representation.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To this end, can I clarify perhaps, was there at any time in which a Parliamentary Select Committee was considered before this Cabinet Committee was actually organised?

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand that a Parliamentary Select Committee would be a Select Committee of MPs, not Ministers.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But the difference is, looking at Standing Order 101, it allows for bipartisan representation.

sections.label: Parliamentary commissioner conflict of interest
sections.summary: A suggestion was made, which the speaker would support, for a Parliamentary commissioner to engage where a conflict of interest appears.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A suggestion, for example, has been made, and I would support this proposal as well, whether there should be a Parliamentary commissioner, perhaps not a standing institution, but a Parliamentary commissioner who could, from time to time, engage where there is an appearance of a conflict of interest.

sections.label: Public consultation on 38 Oxley
sections.summary: The speaker cites a Black Box poll where a majority of close to 1,000 respondents voted to demolish the house, and asks if the Government intends public consultation.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On the other hand, I understand that in a poll conducted by Black Box research, a local market research consultancy, a significant majority of close to 1,000 respondents voted that the house should be demolished in the event a Court were to declare that Mr Lee Kuan Yew was of sound mind, had acted without undue influence, and knew and approved of the contents of that final will.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Of course, these two examples may be anecdotal, they may not be representative examples.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But given that as many of us agree in this House that the fate of 38 Oxley has become a matter of public interest, and if it is a matter of public interest, does the Government intend to include the public in some form of consultation?

sections.label: Committee questions on Lee house
sections.summary: The speaker raises questions about the Committee seeking the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew's children's views, its letter, its undisclosed composition, and the Minister for Law's advice.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It calls to mind the Heritage Master Plan that was spoken about during the Committee of Supply debate earlier this year.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And I understand that the Heritage Master Plan, or at least the first stage, will be released in 2018, and that it will be a five-year plan.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is not about family dispute, as sad as that may be.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But what Singaporeans want is to protect their heritage, to protect their sense of identity, to know who and what they belong to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, why did the Committee find it necessary to seek views from the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew's children to get a clearer sense of his thinking in relation to the house in 2016 when his views, as expressed in his last will, were already made public?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Third, noting the letter dated 27 July 2016 from Minister Lawrence Wong to the executors, in the paragraph which states, "the Committee will be listing the different options and the implications of those options and setting them out in the context of Mr Lee's wishes", my question is: was it contemplated that the children of Mr Lee would be approached to provide their own views on these options and, if so, was it conveyed to his children?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Fourth, why did the Committee decide not to disclose its composition of members, save for Deputy Prime Minister Teo and Minister Lawrence Wong, to Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling at the time when they were asked to provide their views about the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew's thinking and wishes in relation to the house?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Fifth, did the Minister for Law advise the late Mr Lee or any of his family members on matters in connection with the house prior to becoming a member of the Committee?

sections.label: Economic restructuring involvement
sections.summary: The speaker describes five years of involvement in restructuring the Singapore economy and says economic transformation is not easy amid a fluctuating global economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, I had had the opportunity to get involved in the work of restructuring the Singapore economy, from the initial National Productivity Council, to the Council for Skills, Innovation and Productivity, and to the present Future Economy Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am deeply aware that economic transformation is not easy, especially since the global economy is in a state of flux.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At this time, it is even more critical for the Government and the people to stay united in purpose.

sections.label: Lee Kuan Yew legacy value
sections.summary: Putting national interests above personal honour is the most precious value and legacy left by Mr Lee Kuan Yew.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Putting national interests above personal honour − this is the most precious value and legacy left behind by Mr Lee Kuan Yew.

sections.label: Prime Minister court decision
sections.summary: The Prime Minister had decided not to pursue this matter in Court.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Prime Minister, you had decided not to pursue this matter in Court.

sections.label: Probate granted will valid
sections.summary: As probate has been granted and there is no challenge, the will should be taken as valid and proper.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: As the grant of probate has been granted and there is no challenge, the will should be taken as valid and proper.

sections.label: Clarify statutory declaration intentions
sections.summary: A question asks why it was necessary to affirm the statutory declaration and the intentions in doing so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Could you, therefore, clarify why you found it necessary to affirm the statutory declaration and your intentions in doing so?

sections.label: NHB accepted strange exhibition terms
sections.summary: A question asks why NHB proceeded to accept the terms and the exhibition given the conditions appeared strange.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Given that the conditions appeared strange, may I know why NHB proceeded to accept the terms and proceeded with the exhibition?

sections.label: PAP MPs questioning ability closure
sections.summary: PAP MPs' ability to set aside deference to the Prime Minister and ask questions is questioned, and many wish for closure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Even the PAP MPs are not spared as our ability to put aside our deference to the Prime Minister and ask questions on behalf of our constituents are also put to question.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Recently, many I spoke to have expressed their wish that there be closure to the matter.

sections.label: Abuse of power claims unanswered
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Lee siblings to be specific and says no one has interviewed the two whistleblowers for proof.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In particular, if Dr Lee Wei Ling or Mr Lee Hsien Yang claims abuse of power, I would ask that they be more specific and put it up for Prime Minister Lee to answer them and not say later that they were not given the opportunity to put up their part of the story." I believe the Prime Minister and the Ministers will do their best in addressing the questions and I hope that the questions raised can be answered as thoroughly as possible so that any concerns of abuse of powers are allayed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: But at the end of the day, it is up to us to place our faith and trust on the leaders that we have elected to do right by us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While waiting for this EOGM, individual directors rebut the whistleblowers' claims or the purported whistleblowers' claims on Facebook.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, no one − no independent director, no special auditor, no consultant, no member of management, no Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau (CPIB) or law enforcement officer − has met and interviewed the two self-styled whistleblowers to ask them for proof, to interrogate their claims and investigate their veracity.

sections.label: Allegations of abuse of power
sections.summary: The passage lists allegations of abuse of power and notes the Prime Minister acknowledged damage to Singapore's reputation and confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The allegations of abuse of power that have been made include, among other things: the abuse of a Ministerial Committee to pursue a personal agenda; the improper use of a document obtained in a public capacity in private capacity; allegations of intermeddling and appropriation of items without the permission of the estate by the Prime Minister's wife; allegations of the influence of the Prime Minister's wife on governmental functions; allegations of the Government surveilling and harassing the accusers, turning their lives into "an Orwellian nightmare." The Prime Minister has acknowledged that this controversy has damaged the reputation of Singapore for institutional probity and Singaporeans' confidence in the Government.

sections.label: Fact-finding before confidence questions
sections.summary: No one should be asked about confidence in the Government without a fact-finding process allowing accusers to testify and be cross-examined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: No one should be asked, "Do you want the Prime Minister to resign, do you have confidence in the current Government, yes or no?" without the benefit of a fact-finding process that allows the accusers to testify and be cross-examined, together with other persons of interest.

sections.label: Committee asks for statutory declarations
sections.summary: The Committee wrote to Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling asking if they would file statutory declarations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Committee wrote to Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling on this question and asked if they would file statutory declarations on the same.

sections.label: Support for Parliamentary Select Committee
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with MP Pritam Singh's call for a Parliamentary Select Committee to determine facts and recommend follow-up action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: My colleague MP Pritam Singh has eloquently argued for an additional method which is a Parliamentary Select Committee, a call to which I agree and a call to which I think several other Members have also expressed some degree of support today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Such a Committee would have the advantage of leading a process that could determine the facts and recommend follow-up action to Parliament.

sections.label: Call for televised fact-finding hearings
sections.summary: The speaker calls for a Parliamentary Select Committee with televised hearings on abuse of power, and the Committee studies options for the house.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But there seem to be some serious national issues that need to be addressed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We will have to hear all sides out." Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, let us have a Parliamentary Select Committee process with televised hearings on the issues of abuse of power, or some other form of public, interrogative fact-finding with the accusers present, to finally put this matter to bed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On what to do with the house in the future, the Committee is studying a range of options.

sections.label: Independent lawyer drafting will
sections.summary: The law requires the lawyer drafting a will to be independent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Under our law, the lawyer drafting the will is required to be independent.

sections.label: Independent advice issue not for Cabinet
sections.summary: Whether he was independently advised is a serious issue, but the Ministerial Committee or Cabinet does not decide it.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: So, the issue of whether he was independently advised is a serious issue.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: However, it is not for the Ministerial Committee or Cabinet to decide on this issue, nor is the Ministerial Committee or Cabinet attempting to do so.

sections.label: Committee not conducting investigation
sections.summary: The Committee is not investigating and does not decide whose claims are valid, Deputy Prime Minister Teo said.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: You cannot hear one side without hearing the other.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: But the Committee is not conducting an investigation, and Deputy Prime Minister Teo made it clear that it is not for the Committee to decide whose claims are valid.

sections.label: AG and Deputy AG conflicts
sections.summary: The AG and Deputy AG Hri Kumar will not be involved where there is any conflict.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The AG and Deputy AG Hri Kumar will not be involved where there is any conflict.

sections.label: Wong's AG appointment process
sections.summary: Mr Wong's appointment as AG followed a thorough process, with the CPA and President supporting it.
