sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Mr Wong's appointment as AG was decided after a thorough and rigorous process.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Council of Presidential Advisers (CPA) unanimously advised that the President concur with the appointment; and the President, acting in his discretion, also supported it.

sections.label: Shanmugam not consulted as lawyer
sections.summary: Minister Shanmugam was already a Cabinet Minister and was not consulted as a lawyer or adviser.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: At that time, Minister Shanmugam was already a Cabinet Minister.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: He was not consulted as a lawyer and did not advise them as clients.

sections.label: Ministerial Committee options for Cabinet
sections.summary: The Ministerial Committee is not deciding anything and is presenting options for Cabinet to consider.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Ministerial Committee is not making any decisions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: It is putting up a range of options for Cabinet to look at.

sections.label: CPIB and unsubstantiated allegations
sections.summary: The CPIB cannot be expected to look into unsubstantiated allegations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The CPIB cannot be expected to look into unsubstantiated allegations.

sections.label: Lee siblings' allegations lack evidence
sections.summary: Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling have made many allegations, but no substance or evidence has been seen.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling have made plenty of allegations, but we have not seen any substance and no evidence.

sections.label: AG and Deputy AG conflicts
sections.summary: The AG and Deputy AG do not advise the Government on matters they previously handled, and Mr Lucien Wong is not advising the Ministerial Committee on 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: On the first question, the short answer is that the AG and the Deputy AG are not advising the Government on any matters in which they have previously been involved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In other words, whatever it is that they may, in private practice, have advised people on, when they come into the AGC and if it impacts on those areas, then they would not advise on it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, if the Member's question is, for example, is Mr Lucien Wong advising the Ministerial Committee on 38 Oxley Road, the answer is no.

sections.label: AG recusal from past matters
sections.summary: If a matter the AG or Deputy AG acted on in private practice comes up at the AGC, they cannot and will not advise the Government on it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: If there is any matter on which the AG or Deputy AG have acted on when they were in private practice and, if that same matter comes up when they are in AGC, they obviously cannot advise the Government on it and they will not do so.

sections.label: No impropriety found
sections.summary: As far as the speaker can see, there has been no form of impropriety, appearance or otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Because as far as I can see, there has been no form of impropriety, appearance or otherwise.

sections.label: AG appointment due process
sections.summary: The Prime Minister consulted the Chief Justice, Public Service Commission Chairman and incumbent AG before appointing the AG, so due process was observed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: On the second part, on appointments, as I had said earlier, when the AG was appointed, the Prime Minister consulted the Chief Justice, he consulted the Chairman of the Public Service Commission, as well as the incumbent AG on the appointment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Due process was observed and there is absolutely nothing wrong with the current appointment of the AG.

sections.label: Low and Lim raise AG issue
sections.summary: Mr Low and Ms Sylvia Lim keep raising the issue, but there is no basis for concern that the AG acted improperly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Indeed, it is only Mr Low and Ms Sylvia Lim who keep raising this issue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: There is no basis for any concern that the AG has not acted in a manner that is entirely proper.

sections.label: Ministerial Statements on allegations
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee and Deputy Prime Minister Teo issued Ministerial Statements on the allegations and the Cabinet committees' rationale, and Lee recused himself from Oxley Road deliberations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lee and Deputy Prime Minister Teo had issued Ministerial Statements on these allegations and the rationale for the setting up of the Cabinet committees yesterday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lee also stated that he had recused himself from deliberations about Oxley Road.

sections.label: Oxley Road property sale question
sections.summary: A question asks the Prime Minister about offering to sell Oxley Road to Dr Lee Wei Ling for $1, then selling to Mr Lee Hsien Yang at market value and asking for half to charity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Next, I wish to ask the Prime Minister about his Ministerial Statement that he offered to sell the Oxley Road property to Dr Lee Wei Ling for $1 but later sold it to Mr Lee Hsien Yang for the full market value?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In addition, the Prime Minister asked him to donate half of the value of the property to charity.

sections.label: Oxley Road demolition insistence
sections.summary: Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling insisted 38 Oxley Road be demolished as stated by Mr Lee Kuan Yew in the seventh will dated 17 December 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling were insistent that 38 Oxley Road is to be demolished as stated by Mr Lee Kuan Yew in the seventh will dated 17 December 2013.

sections.label: Statutory declaration on seventh will
sections.summary: The Prime Minister issued a statutory declaration on 15 June 2017 questioning the circumstances behind the making of the seventh will.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In response, the Prime Minister issued a statutory declaration on 15 June 2017 questioning the circumstances behind the making of the seventh will.

sections.label: Lawyer acting for testator rule
sections.summary: Rule 46 of the Legal Profession (Professional Conduct) Rules prohibits a lawyer from acting for a testator intending a significant gift to the lawyer's family member.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Second – and here, I wear my hat as a practising lawyer – rule 46 of the Legal Profession (Professional Conduct) Rules prohibits a lawyer from acting for a testator who intends to make a significant gift to any member of the family of that lawyer.

sections.label: Independent advice on will
sections.summary: The speaker questions whether Minister Mentor Lee, aged 89 or 90, was independently advised on the will, which may affect the demolition clause's validity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: My concern is whether Minister Mentor Lee, at age 89 or 90 at that time, was independently advised about the contents of the will.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This is of legal significance because it may mean that the demolition clause in the will may not be valid and it will affect the way the Government assesses the intent of Minister Mentor Lee about the demolition clause.

sections.label: Will contradicts development application
sections.summary: If Minister Mentor Lee authorised the March 2012 development application for 38 Oxley Road, the will's demolition clause seems to contradict his position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: If Minister Mentor Lee had in March 2012 authorised his architects to submit the development application for 38 Oxley Road, then the demolition clause in the will seems to contradict Minister Mentor's position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Government should look further into the circumstances behind the making of the last will and, in particular, whether Mr Lee Kuan Yew was independently advised when he signed the last will.

sections.label: Disagreement is not abuse of power
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee disagreeing with the siblings' proposal to demolish the house does not mean there is abuse of power.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Just because Prime Minister Lee does not agree with the siblings' proposal to demolish the house does not in any way mean that there is abuse of power.

sections.label: Lee Kuan Yew and mediation hope
sections.summary: Mr Lee Kuan Yew helped shape ideas and values and made Singapore successful, and the speaker hopes for private mediation instead of public accusations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew helped shaped our ideas, our values and, with his team of leaders, made Singapore successful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I truly hope that there can be some resolution to this matter through private mediation instead of having more public accusations hurled against the Prime Minister.

sections.label: Questions on PSD survey
sections.summary: The speaker asks what the results of the PSD survey of public officers were and whether concrete follow-up action will be taken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, keep my speech very brief and just ask two questions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: It was reported that the Public Service Division (PSD) sent out a survey to public officers on the dispute over 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: While PSD said this was because the allegations made went beyond private matters, some questions remain as to whether this sort of poll was appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: Could the Minister clarify as to: (a) what were the results of the poll?

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: (c) whether there is any concrete action that will be taken to follow up on the results of the poll.

sections.label: Prime Minister's 38 Oxley Road finances
sections.summary: The Prime Minister gained no money from the transaction, holds no interest in 38 Oxley Road, and a sum about one and a half times its value went to charity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For the Prime Minister, there was no personal financial gain from the transaction and he now also has no financial interest in 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Quite the reverse, a substantial sum of money, the equivalent of about one and a half times the property value of 38 Oxley Road actually went into charity and for a very good cause.

sections.label: July 2011 Lee Kuan Yew Cabinet meeting
sections.summary: A Member asks the Prime Minister and Deputy Prime Minister what happened at the 14 July 2011 meeting between Mr Lee Kuan Yew and the Cabinet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I hope the Prime Minister and the Ministers can give a comprehensive and complete reply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But I have one additional point of doubt which I would like to ask the Deputy Prime Minister, and that is, what transpired in the meeting between the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew and the Cabinet on 14 July 2011.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: He felt that he should not have listened to the Prime Minister to meet with the Cabinet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Prime Minister and the Deputy Prime Minister whether the Cabinet exerted pressure on Mr Lee Kuan Yew at that time to give up his idea of demolishing the house, or whether they told or misled Mr Lee Kuan Yew that the Government would preserve the house, regardless of his views.

sections.label: 38 Oxley Road identity and legacy
sections.summary: A Member says 38 Oxley Road matters for national identity and legacy, notes Dr Lee Wei Ling wishes to live there, and hopes the dispute does not distract from pressing issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: From the point of national identity and historical legacy, 38 Oxley Road is definitely important to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What is more, Dr Lee Wei Ling has expressed the wish to continue living there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, I hope the Government will not have its attention divided by this dispute, because there are more pressing issues, such as the economy, security, employment and an ageing population.

sections.label: Parliament should investigate
sections.summary: Parliament should get to the bottom of it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Parliament should get to the bottom of it.

sections.label: Mencius quote on Prime Minister
sections.summary: Quoting Mencius, a Member says the Prime Minister has put the country and system before himself and his family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Mencius said that "people come first, the country second and the king, last." From this incident we can see that the Prime Minister, in all his decisions and dealings, has put the country and the system before himself and his family.

sections.label: Allegations of abuse of power
sections.summary: The issue before Parliament is not preservation or demolition but allegations by Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling of abuse of power.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The issue before Parliament, as several Members had pointed out, is not about the preservation or demolition of the house, but rather, the allegations directed at the Prime Minister and the Government by Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling of an abuse of power.

sections.label: No abuse of power found
sections.summary: The speaker states there has been no abuse of power and no specific allegations against the Prime Minister and Government requiring deeper inquiry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: My own view is: no, there has been no abuse of power.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have heard no specific allegations of acts of abuse against the Prime Minister and the Government that demand a deeper inquiry.

sections.label: Lee's views on 38 Oxley Road
sections.summary: In July 2011, Mr Lee came to the Cabinet meeting to set out his views on 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In July 2011, Mr Lee came to the Cabinet meeting to set out his views on 38 Oxley Road.

sections.label: Cabinet unanimous on not demolishing
sections.summary: Except for the Prime Minister who did not speak, Cabinet members were unanimous in persuading him the house should not be demolished.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Except for the Prime Minister who did not speak, Cabinet members were unanimous in persuading him that the house should not be demolished.

sections.label: Lee Kuan Yew Fund for Bilingualism
sections.summary: In 2011 he decided to set up a fund with his own money and brought in other donors, and with his approval it was named the Lee Kuan Yew Fund for Bilingualism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In 2011, he decided to set up a fund, with his own money, and brought in several other donors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With his approval, I named it the Lee Kuan Yew Fund for Bilingualism.

sections.label: Lee's plan and last letter
sections.summary: Mr Lee had a plan and put it into action, and his December 2011 letter saying the whole building should be refurbished if preserved was the last communication Cabinet received on the subject.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This shows that Mr Lee had a plan and he put it into action.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: That letter of December 2011, in which he said the whole building should be refurbished "if 38 Oxley Road is to be preserved", was the last communication Cabinet received from Mr Lee on this subject.

sections.label: Lee's memoirs preface on government
sections.summary: In his memoirs preface, Mr Lee wrote he wrote the book for younger Singaporeans who took stability, growth and prosperity for granted, and that an honest and effective government is achieved only by years of dedicated effort.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In the preface to his memoirs, Mr Lee wrote, "I wrote this book for a younger generation of Singaporeans who took stability, growth and prosperity for granted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I wanted them to know how difficult it was for a small country of 640 square kilometres with no natural resources to survive in the midst of larger, newly independent nations all pursuing nationalistic policies… we cannot forget that public order, personal security, economic and social progress and prosperity are not the natural order of things, that they depend on ceaseless effort and attention from an honest and effective government that the people must elect." An honest and effective government is a simple and powerful idea, but one that is achieved only by years of dedicated effort.

sections.label: Cabinet meetings and debate
sections.summary: Cabinet meetings and other forums have deliberated on these issues, and the speaker hopes two days of debate will clear the air and rebuild trust.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Various Cabinet meetings and other forums have been deliberating on these various issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I hope these two days of debate can help clear the air, rebuild trust and confidence, so that everyone can focus fully on the challenges that we face.

sections.label: 38 Oxley Road and Singapore
sections.summary: A future government may demolish 38 Oxley Road as the founding Prime Minister wished, but Lee Kuan Yew also built Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In the years to come, when Dr Lee Wei Ling is no longer living at 38 Oxley Road, a future government may agree to demolish the house, as our founding Prime Minister wished.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: But there is another house that Mr Lee Kuan Yew built lovingly, a greater house than 38 Oxley Road − and that is Singapore.

sections.label: Contempt of Parliament question
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether Lee Hsien Yang's accusations that this Parliament session clouds truth or hides wrongdoings can be deemed contempt of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: Here, I would like to ask whether Mr Lee Hsien Yang's accusations that this Parliament session is held to cloud the truth or hide wrongdoings can be deemed as contempt of Parliament.

sections.label: Select Committee and statutory declaration
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Prime Minister to state his position on a Select Committee and why he made a statutory declaration on the last will.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: Some have also suggested setting up a Select Committee to look into the allegations levelled by the Prime Minister's siblings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: I hope that the Prime Minister can state his position on such a Select Committee in order to dismiss any negative perceptions that the Government wants to suppress the truth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: Regarding the will, I would like to ask the Prime Minister why he made a statutory declaration on the circumstances that led to the last will.

sections.label: Checks against abuse of power
sections.summary: The speaker asks what checks and balances in Government ensure conflicts of interest and abuse of power are avoided.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: Furthermore, I would like to ask, from a national governance perspective, what are the checks and balances that exist in Government to ensure that conflicts of interest and abuse of power are avoided and do not take root in our governance structure?

sections.label: Lee family feud over 38 Oxley Road
sections.summary: The subject is the Lee Kuan Yew family feud over 38 Oxley Road and the allegation of abuse of power by the Prime Minister and colleagues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The subject matter is none other than the family feud of the late Lee Kuan Yew's family with regard to the property at 38 Oxley Road and the allegation of the abuse of power of our Prime Minister and his colleagues.

sections.label: Investigating allegations against Public Service
sections.summary: The speaker urges further investigation by an Independent Committee or Commission of Inquiry so accusers can present evidence and the matter is handled transparently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While there is neither clear nor conclusive evidence provided hitherto by the accusers, I would like to suggest that we treat it seriously and launch further investigations into this matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We should allow the accusers to present their case and provide evidence to an Independent Committee or Commission of Inquiry so as to ensure open and fair treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It will be our duty as parliamentarians and lawmakers to ensure that such serious matters are properly dealt with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe every Singaporean has the right to know and hear the full extent of this important matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am of the opinion that failure to address this allegation and to handle it with utmost transparency and impartiality may lead to a retardation of trust in our Public Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Henceforth, I urge the House and the relevant authority to take a similar stand in ensuring that the image and excellent reputation of our Public Service institution are safeguarded.

sections.label: Integrity and trust in government
sections.summary: The passage states that the core issue for Parliament is integrity and trust in the Prime Minister and the system of government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Chok Tong (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The nub of the issue for us in Parliament is integrity and trust − in the Prime Minister and our system of government.

sections.label: Lee Hsien Yang's goal
sections.summary: The passage states that Lee Hsien Yang and his wife aim to bring Lee Hsien Loong down as Prime Minister despite collateral damage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Chok Tong (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: From what Lee Hsien Yang and his wife are freely telling many people, it is clear that their goal is to bring Lee Hsien Loong down as Prime Minister, regardless of the huge collateral damage suffered by the Government and Singaporeans.

sections.label: Clearing or censuring the Prime Minister
sections.summary: The passage states that Parliament must either clear the Prime Minister over the abuse of power allegation or censure him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Chok Tong (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Either we clear Prime Minister over the allegation of his abuse of power or we censure him.

sections.label: Confidence in Prime Minister's integrity
sections.summary: The speaker says he heard Members' views and reaffirms full confidence in the integrity of the Prime Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Chok Tong (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I have heard the views and questions of Members, and paid close attention to those from the Workers' Party and the Nominated Members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Chok Tong (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I reaffirm my full confidence in the integrity of the Prime Minister.

sections.label: Accounts and Deputy Prime Minister Teo
sections.summary: The speaker says the Prime Minister's and Deputy Prime Minister's accounts match his knowledge and that Deputy Prime Minister Teo acted independently as Committee Chairman.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Chok Tong (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: On this case, the Prime Minister's and Deputy Prime Minister's accounts accord with my knowledge of how the Government and Ministers operate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Chok Tong (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I am also fully satisfied that Deputy Prime Minister Teo acted independently as Chairman of the Ministerial Committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Chok Tong (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I met him in June 2016 to understand his thinking of a possible range of options for 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Chok Tong (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I was trying to mediate between the Prime Minister and Lee Hsien Yang.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Chok Tong (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I conveyed Deputy Prime Minister's thinking to Hsien Yang on 23 June last year.

sections.label: Allegations called baseless
sections.summary: The passage states that after statements from both sides and the Government, the allegations are clearly baseless.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Chok Tong (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: After so much has been said by both sides and the Government, it is clear that the allegations are baseless.

sections.label: Prime Minister accused, no investigation
sections.summary: It contrasts Goh Chok Tong's earlier investigation and Parliament explanation with this session, where the Prime Minister is accused and no investigation was done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: It was the then Prime Minister Mr Goh Chok Tong who called for investigation based on the market rumour and then came to Parliament for the public explanation and the debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: But for this Parliament session, it is the Prime Minister, the head of the Government and the Secretary-General of the PAP, who is accused of wrongdoing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: In this episode, there is no investigation done, it is "own self defend own self" in Parliament with the PAP Members of Parliament.

sections.label: Goh Chok Tong sued Tang Liang Hong
sections.summary: It asks whether the former Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong has forgotten suing Workers' Party candidate Tang Liang Hong in 1997 over a police report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: Has he forgotten that the former Prime Minister ─ Mr Goh Chok Tong who is now Emeritus Senior Minister ─ sued the Workers' Party candidate Tang Liang Hong during the General Elections in 1997 for just making a police report?

sections.label: Veiled threat over questions
sections.summary: It says Png Eng Huat is right that the Prime Minister called the session, and notes a veiled threat from Indranee Rajah about asking questions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: I have some difficulty understanding because, first of all, Mr Png Eng Huat is right.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: This session is called by the Prime Minister and he said, "I will give a Ministerial Statement, please question me rigorously." But then we heard a veiled threat yesterday from Indranee Rajah that you are making allegations when you are asking some questions.

sections.label: 38 Oxley Road public interest
sections.summary: It says the future of 38 Oxley Road, home of the founding Prime Minister and centre of the dispute, is of major public interest.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: He led by example, living simply and frugally at 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Therefore, the future of 38 Oxley Road, the home of our founding Prime Minister, and the centre of the current dispute between our Prime Minister and his siblings, is not a private matter but one which is of major public interest.

sections.label: Preserve 38 Oxley Road
sections.summary: It suggests the Government preserve 38 Oxley Road to remind Singaporeans of the Founding Father and what he stood for.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: It has meaning for all Singaporeans – past, present and future.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I respectfully suggest to the Government that 38 Oxley Road be preserved to remind us of our Founding Father and what he stood for.

sections.label: Prime Minister house transfer question
sections.summary: A Member asks the Prime Minister why he offered to transfer the house to his sister for $1 and sold it to his brother at full value.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Like other Members, I want to ask the Prime Minister why did he offer to transfer the house to his sister for $1 and why did he sell it to his brother at full value?

sections.label: Drawer plans and resident
sections.summary: A Member asks how drawer plans would affect residents while Dr Lee Wei Ling continues to reside in the house.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Given that Deputy Prime Minister Teo has said in his Ministerial Statement that the Committee is only coming up with "drawer plans", how would such plans affect the residents there going forward, whilst and during the period that Dr Lee Wei Ling continues to reside in the house?

sections.label: Siblings' allegations and next step
sections.summary: A Member asks what the Prime Minister and Government's next step would be if his siblings continue publicly airing allegations of abuse of power.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: First, we know it takes two parties, at least in this case, to bring a conflict to closure.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Post this Parliamentary debate, if the Prime Minister's siblings refuse to back down and continue to publicly air their allegations of abuse of power by the Prime Minister, what would the Prime Minister and the Government's next step be?

sections.label: Moving forward and heritage buildings
sections.summary: A Member asks how the country moves forward and how NHB looks out for potential architectures, particularly privately owned ones, informing owners before decisions.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: How then do we move forward as a country if we cannot see beyond these differences?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: And lastly, yesterday, Minister Lawrence Wong mentioned that there are 72 buildings gazetted for preservation and 7,000 others conserved to date.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: How does National Heritage Board (NHB) actively look out for potential architectures that are likely to be preserved, particularly those privately owned, and inform the private owners duly with ample time before a decision is made?

sections.label: Executors' non-negotiable buyback provision
sections.summary: The $1 buyback provision was non-negotiable per the executors' lawyer, and NHB had to sign the Deed on stipulated terms or do without the artefacts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The $1 buyback provision was, as the lawyer of the executors said, to quote, "non-negotiable".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But the executors required this to be displayed prominently in other areas of the exhibition as well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, given the executors' position, NHB really had just two choices − either sign the Deed on the stipulated terms or do without the artefacts completely.

sections.label: NHB decision to sign Deed
sections.summary: NHB deliberated and eventually decided to sign the Deed because of several considerations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: NHB deliberated over this and they decided eventually to sign the Deed because of several considerations.

sections.label: Oxley Road research work oversight
sections.summary: Oxley Road research work is ongoing among agencies and overseen by a Ministerial Committee ensuring comprehensive and rigorous due diligence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For Oxley Road, this research work is ongoing amongst the various agencies and, the work, as we have discussed, is being overseen by the Ministerial Committee which will ensure that the due diligence work done is comprehensive and rigorous.

sections.label: Approaching executors to postpone exhibition
sections.summary: Recognising differences in views among beneficiaries, the executors were approached to see if the August exhibition could be put off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Recognising that there were differences in views amongst the beneficiaries, we approached the executors to see if we could put off the exhibition in August.

sections.label: Further update to Prime Minister
sections.summary: After NHB's statement that night on outstanding questions, a further update was given to the Prime Minister on events since 8 June 2015, including the Deed of Gift specifics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: NHB then also had to put out a statement that same night to say that there were questions that were still outstanding, that we were seeking resolution from the executors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, being mindful that all these had been playing out after my last update to the Prime Minister on 8 June 2015 I had to give him a further update, naturally at that time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: He did not ask me, but I had to give him a further update on the matter, telling him what had happened since 8 June 2015, and giving him the full facts of the information, including the specifics of the Deed of Gift.

sections.label: Clarifying roles and conflict rules
sections.summary: With hindsight, some roles ought to have been better clarified, and NHB strengthened internal processes to ensure conflict rules are observed within the Board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Again, with the benefit of hindsight, some of these roles ought to have been better clarified and NHB has, indeed, strengthened its own processes internally to make sure that conflict rules are observed within the Board.

sections.label: Focus of the debate
sections.summary: The debate focuses on the integrity of Government, conflict of interest, any basis for abuse of power allegations, and where to go from here.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The debate is, first and foremost, focused on the integrity of Government − whether we have clean and honest Government, and how we address issues of conflict of interest; second, whether there is any basis for the allegations of abuse of power that have been hurled at the Government; and third, where do we go from here?

sections.label: PSD poll on allegations
sections.summary: PSD conducted the poll because the allegations extend to the integrity of Government and public institutions, with most officers seeing some impact on credibility that can recover.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The PSD conducted the poll because the allegations made by Dr Lee Wei Ling and Mr Lee Hsien Yang go beyond private matters and extend to the integrity of the Government and public institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Most officers felt that there is some impact on credibility of the Singapore Government among Singaporeans, but that Singapore's reputation will be able to recover.

sections.label: Discomfort with Deed conditions
sections.summary: The speaker was not comfortable with the conditions set out in the Deed when Minister Lawrence Wong informed them.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: When Minister Lawrence Wong informed me of the conditions set out in the Deed, I was not comfortable with them.

sections.label: Proceeding with signed Deed of Gift
sections.summary: NHB had signed the Deed of Gift and the speaker agreed with Minister Lawrence Wong to proceed rather than have a public controversy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: NHB had already signed the Deed of Gift and I agreed with Minister Lawrence Wong that in the circumstances, we should proceed with it, rather than have a public controversy.

sections.label: Members speaking on Ministerial Committee
sections.summary: Several named Members spoke on the Ministerial Committee, which was formed to examine the property's significance, Mr Lee Kuan Yew's wishes and possible plans.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, Ms Sun Xueling, Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Louis Ng, Ms Jessica Tan, Dr Tan Wu Meng, Mr Christopher de Souza, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin, Ms Rahayu Mahzam, Mr Low Thia Khiang, Mr Murali Pillai, Mr Leon Perera and some others today as well, have spoken on the Ministerial Committee.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: I explained that the Ministerial Committee was formed to examine (a) historical and heritage significance of the property; (b) the wishes of Mr Lee Kuan Yew in relation to the property; and (c) the possible plans for the property and the neighbourhood, and the options to move forward.

sections.label: Ministerial Committee not replacing agencies
sections.summary: Several Members asked why a Ministerial Committee was set up instead of the usual agency process, and the speaker clarified it is not replacing the agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Several Members, Mr Low Thia Khiang, Mr Kok Heng Leun, Mr Zaqy Mohamad, Mr Louis Ng, Mr Leon Perera have asked why we set up a Ministerial Committee and not rely on the usual Government agency process to study the options on the house?

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: I want to clarify that the Ministerial Committee is not replacing the agencies in their work.

sections.label: Lee Hsien Loong conveying private views
sections.summary: Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked if the Prime Minister influenced decisions, but Mr Lee Hsien Loong was invited as a private person to convey views like his siblings.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked whether the Prime Minister had any influence on the Cabinet or Ministerial Committee's decisions.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: But Mr Lee Hsien Loong, as a private person, was invited to convey his views to the Ministerial Committee in the same way that his other siblings were.

sections.label: Prime Minister recused himself
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee did the correct thing to recuse himself, and Cabinet and the Government carried out their roles and responsibilities properly.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lee did the correct thing to recuse himself.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: And Cabinet and the Government carried out its roles and responsibilities properly.

sections.label: No decision required now
sections.summary: Mr Lee Hsien Yang acknowledges no decision is required now because Dr Lee Wei Ling continues to live in the property.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Mr Lee Hsien Yang also acknowledges that no decision is required now because Dr Lee Wei Ling continues to live in the property.

sections.label: Wei Ling's right to live
sections.summary: The Government said it will not do anything to affect Wei Ling's right to continue living at 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: For Wei Ling, the Government has said that we will not do anything to affect her right to continue living at 38 Oxley Road.

sections.label: No one above the law
sections.summary: No one is above the law, Mr Lee abided by the system, and he left Singapore to all.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: No one is above the law, or bigger than our collective interest, as Ms Chia Yong Yong has passionately pointed out.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Mr Lee himself understood that he, too, had to abide by the processes and system that he helped build; and that the Government has a duty to consider the public interest and not just those of private individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: But most of all, he taught us, all of us, to uphold these principles.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We have not been written into Mr Lee's will.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: But what he has left to all of us, is more precious, more valuable.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: He left us Our Singapore, Our big house, which he worked together with us to build.

sections.label: Allegations of abusing power answered
sections.summary: The allegations about abusing power have been answered and no Members produced or substantiated additional facts or charges.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Over the past two days, the allegations about me abusing power, which prompted the sitting, have been answered.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: No Members have produced or alleged any additional facts or charges, or substantiated any of the allegations.

sections.label: No conflict for appointments
sections.summary: Because he has old cases that may appear before the Courts, there is no conflict for Lucien Wong or Hri Kumar.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Because he has old cases and cases may appear before the Courts and he cannot participate in the cases when they turn up before the Courts.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: So, there is no problem of conflict at all for Lucien Wong or Hri Kumar to become AG and DAG.

sections.label: AG appointment needs President's approval
sections.summary: The AG's appointment has to be confirmed and approved by the President.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The AG's appointment has to be confirmed, approved by the President.

sections.label: Malaysia ICJ Pedra Branca application
sections.summary: Malaysia filed an application over the ICJ judgment on Pedra Branca, which the speaker says has no merit but needs a top-notch team.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Four days ago, on 30 June, Malaysia filed an application over the ICJ judgment on Pedra Branca.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We think the Malaysian case has no merit but, unless we have a top-notch team, we may mishandle the case with very serious consequences.

sections.label: Denial of deceiving father
sections.summary: The speaker states simply that he did not deceive his father.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The simple answer is that I did not deceive my father.

sections.label: Father wills house to speaker
sections.summary: In August 2011 the father decided to will the house to the speaker and told the family.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: In August 2011, about a month later, he decided to will the house to me, as I told Members yesterday, and he told the family.

sections.label: No decision while sister lives
sections.summary: After the father died, the speaker said in Parliament on 13 April 2015 that the Government would take no decision on the house while his sister lived in it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: After my father died, I said in Parliament on 13 April 2015, as I recounted yesterday, that the Government will take no decision on the house, so long as my sister was living in it.

sections.label: Offer house to sister for $1
sections.summary: Learning his siblings were unhappy, the speaker offered in May 2015 to transfer the house to his sister for a nominal $1.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: When I learnt from others, who were meant to tell me, that my siblings were unhappy that my father had willed me the house, I tried to resolve the unhappiness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: So, in May 2015, I offered to transfer the house to my sister for a nominal sum of $1.

sections.label: Condition on sale proceeds charity
sections.summary: The speaker let his sister own the house on condition that sale or government acquisition proceeds be donated to charity, and another wanted to jointly buy it for $1.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: So, it was natural to let her own the house.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I only asked for one condition: that if the property was sold later, or acquired by the Government, that the proceeds would be donated to charity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I thought it was a very reasonable offer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: He wanted to join in and jointly buy the house with my sister from me for $1.

sections.label: Fresh offer to sell house
sections.summary: He made a new offer to sell the house to his brother at full market value, with each donating half to charity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I told my siblings that we were not getting anywhere on the $1 offer, with the conditions on what each side could do or say.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: So, I made them a fresh offer, forget all the previous discussions, new offer, no conditions on what we can do or say, but I will sell the house to my brother at full market value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: And the only condition, which is attached now, is that we each donate half of the value to charity.

sections.label: Explaining last will to committee
sections.summary: He explained the circumstances of preparing the last will to the Ministerial Committee through sworn statutory declarations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: So, I felt the need to explain the circumstances surrounding the preparation of the last will to the Ministerial Committee, so that it would understand what to make of the evidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: And because of the gravity of the matter, I voluntarily made my submissions to the Ministerial Committee in the form of sworn statutory declarations or, as they say in the coffee shops – sumpah.

sections.label: No evidence behind allegations
sections.summary: After two days of debate, nobody, including Opposition Members, stood behind the allegations or offered evidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: After two days of debate, nobody has stood behind these allegations or offered any evidence, not even Opposition Members.

sections.label: Possible steps on emerging evidence
sections.summary: He said vague allegations do not justify a Select Committee or COI, but emerging evidence would lead to further steps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: Vague allegations based on scattered evidence centred on family displeasure, as a basis for ordering a Select Committee or a COI?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: But if there is evidence of wrongdoing which emerges, or alleged evidence of wrongdoing which emerges, then I and the Government will consider what further steps to take.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: We can have a Select Committee, we can have a Commission of Inquiry, I may decide to sue for defamation or take some other legal action.

sections.label: Allegations aired and rebutted
sections.summary: The allegations were aired, answered and rebutted, showing no abuse of power by him or the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: The allegations have been aired, have been answered, rebutted, and people can see that there has been no abuse of power by me or the Government.

sections.label: Purpose to restore public confidence
sections.summary: His purpose was not a family fight but to clear the air and restore public confidence in the system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: My purpose has not been to pursue a family fight, but to clear the air and to restore public confidence in our system.

sections.label: Building safe prosperous Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker says he and his team will do their best to keep building Singapore, keeping it safe and making it prosper.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: My team and I will do our best to continue building this Singapore, keeping it safe and making it prosper.

sections.label: Options for alleged wrongdoing
sections.summary: The speaker says if there is evidence of wrongdoing, he will decide what to do and consider a Committee of Inquiry, Select Committee, defamation or other options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: As I have said, if there is evidence of wrongdoing or serious evidence of alleged wrongdoing, certainly, I will have to decide what to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: And we will have to consider a Committee of Inquiry, a Select Committee, defamation or there may be other options.

sections.label: Selling house if allegations stop
sections.summary: The speaker says he sold the house and will sell it if the other party undertakes to stop the allegations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: That was why I sold you the house.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: So, I will sell you the house if you undertake to stop these allegations".

sections.label: Impasse over house and accusations
sections.summary: The speaker says he cannot sell the house for $1 unless the accusations stop, describing this as the impasse when he dissolved Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I keep my peace or I reserve my right to speak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: But I cannot sell you the house for $1 unless the accusations stop." And that is the impasse and that was the essence of the position when I dissolved Parliament.

sections.label: NHB information to Lee Hsien Loong
sections.summary: The speaker says that if Mr Lee Hsien Loong had written to NHB for information in his private capacity, NHB would have given it to him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Yes, Madam, under the circumstances, I have said that if Mr Lee Hsien Loong, in his private capacity, given his circumstance as a beneficiary of the estate with interest in the assets, had written to NHB for information, NHB would have given him the information.

sections.label: No difference in intent
sections.summary: The speaker says that for all intents and purposes he sees no difference.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Indeed, so, Madam, for all intents and purposes, I see no difference.

sections.label: Ho Ching passing letters to PMO
sections.summary: The Prime Minister's wife, Ho Ching, passed a battleship telegram and three old letters found at 38 Oxley Road to PMO for the NHB exhibition on Mr Lee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: One of the evidence of abuse of power or allegations is that the Prime Minister's wife, Ho Ching, was acting on behalf of the Prime Minister's Office.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: It is a simple matter of a battleship telegram and three old letters which my wife came across in 38 Oxley Road, told me about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I thought they were significant and relevant to the exhibition on Mr Lee which NHB was putting up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: And I facilitated and arranged for her to pass it to PMO and for PMO to send it on to the NHB exhibition.

sections.label: Committee not judging will validity
sections.summary: The Committee told all three siblings it is not its place to determine the validity of the will.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And if we had gone about our work and said, look, you know, Party A said this and Party B said that, and I cannot tell you what Party A said, and I cannot tell you what Party B said, there might also have been reason to be upset.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And we were very, very clear with the siblings, all three of them, that it is not the place of the Committee to determine the validity of the will.

sections.label: Committee understanding Lee's wishes
sections.summary: The Committee seeks to understand Mr Lee's wishes and thinking and will make no judgement on the validity of his will.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We were concerned about the options, we are concerned about the history and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We are not replacing the work of the Probate Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: But we seek to understand what Mr Lee's wishes were, what was Mr Lee's thinking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And we make no judgement, we are not in a position to make judgement and we will not make any judgement on the validity of Mr Lee's will.

sections.label: Ministerial Committee terms of reference
sections.summary: The Ministerial Committee's terms of reference are to look at the range of options and understand Mr Lee's thinking and wishes for the house.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The terms of reference of the Ministerial Committee are also to look at the range of options and to understand Mr Lee's thinking and wishes for the house.

sections.label: No reason to convene inquiry
sections.summary: On the basis of what they have said, there is not a reason to convene a Select Committee or a COI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: And then, we will all be the wiser.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: But as of now, on the basis of what they have said, there is not a reason to convene a Select Committee or a COI.

sections.label: Dr Lee need not move out
sections.summary: It is difficult to say whether it is the last word because of freedom of speech, and Dr Lee does not need to move out now, so no decision is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: Whether it is the last word, that is very difficult to say because there is freedom of speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We agree that Dr Lee does not need to move out now, so no decision is needed.

sections.label: Oxley Road motion lapses
sections.summary: The Motion to consider two Ministerial Statements on 38 Oxley Road lapses at the conclusion of debate, and the Sitting is suspended.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: Pursuant to Standing Order No 44(2), the Motion to consider the two Ministerial Statements on 38 Oxley Road lapses at the conclusion of debate.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
